The test image shows soybean leaves with distinctive white, powdery patches on the upper leaf surface, particularly concentrated near the petiole junction and spreading outward. This strongly points to Powdery Mildew.

Let me view reference images to confirm.
Good match. The reference shows white-gray powdery coating matching what I see in the test image. Let me also check Downy Mildew (which shows on lower surface) and a couple other candidates.

Downy mildew shows yellowish spots on upper surface with gray tufts underneath - different. Frogeye shows circular gray lesions with red-brown borders - different. The test image clearly has white powdery patches on the upper leaf surface.

Let me view a few more references to meet the minimum requirement.

Both confirm they don't match. Septoria shows dark brown spots on yellow leaves; Cercospora shows reddish-purple bronzing.

**Initial prediction: Powdery_Mildew**

The white powdery patches on the upper leaf surface are the definitive diagnostic feature.

Now reading the attractor guide:
Powdery_Mildew is listed as over-predicted. Alternatives are Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (2x) and Soybean_Cyst_Nematode (1x). Let me check these references.

Neither alternative matches. Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus shows green-yellow mottling; Soybean_Cyst_Nematode shows yellowing/stunting with cysts on roots. Neither has white powdery patches.

The test image is unambiguously **Powdery_Mildew**: white powdery coating visible on the upper leaf surfaces, beginning in patches near the petiole and spreading across the leaves, on otherwise green healthy-looking tissue. This matches the reference images and the symptom description perfectly.
